description: The most important news for developers is the critical RCE vulnerability in OpenJDK (Java4Shell) and the continued shift toward autonomous AI agents, evidenced by Apple’s new device-control agents, GitLab’s agentic goal-based automation, and Vercel’s Board coordination primitive. articles.title: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
articles.description: Google's Gemini API introduces Tool Retrieval, enabling dynamic function execution like issuing refunds based on input. Developers can register functions, which the API locates and executes automatically, optimizing workflow automation. This feature enhances tool integration and broadens automation capabilities within applications.
articles.one-liner: Google’s new Tool Retrieval API for Gemini optimizes performance by loading function schemas dynamically instead of forcing agents to hold entire libraries in context.

summary.what: The feature, available in preview in the Gemini Interactions API, allows developers to set defer_loading: true for tool functions. The model accesses only necessary schemas during execution, reducing input token counts and latency while supporting Gemini 3.6+ models.
summary.why: This shift addresses the efficiency wall for agentic workflows where increasingly large tool libraries threaten to exceed context limits and degrade performance.
summary.takeaway: If you are managing large tool sets in Gemini, add a tool_search tool and flag deferred functions to reduce your input token usage.

articles.deep-summary:
* Implements on-demand schema loading to keep prompt context focused.
* Supports both server-side retrieval and custom client-side registries via the tool_search tool.
* Integrates with MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers for remote tool access.
* Leverages prefix caching by keeping stable schemas out of the variable function-call context.
* No additional cost beyond standard model pricing for tokens used.
articles.decoder:
* **Tool Retrieval**: An optimization technique where an AI model dynamically fetches function definitions as needed rather than having them pre-loaded in the context window.
* **MCP (Model Context Protocol)**: An open standard for connecting AI models to external data and tool sources.
* **Prefix Caching**: A feature where the system saves the computation of common, repeated parts of a prompt to speed up future requests.

articles.title: Let Gemini tackle repetitive chores on your Mac
articles.description: Computer use in the Gemini app for Mac can now help users get multi-step tasks done across their local files, desktop apps, and the web. Gemini works inside an isolated background window with a live preview right in the chat. Users' main screen and cursor remain completely free, so they can continue typing, designing, or taking calls without interruption. Users can choose which apps Gemini can access, watch every step live, pause at any time, and approve key actions before they happen.
articles.one-liner: Gemini for Mac can now autonomously drive desktop applications through an isolated background window while leaving the user’s primary workspace untouched.

summary.what: The new computer use capability enables Gemini to perform multi-step tasks like batch processing photos, filling out local PDF forms, or scraping metrics from dashboards, all controlled by user-approved permissions and live visual monitoring.
summary.takeaway: Download the latest Gemini app for Mac to automate multi-app workflows.

articles.title: When Agent Swarms Outperform Solo Coders
articles.description: Replit's optimization benchmark found 32 Opus agents achieved an 18.9× NumPy workload speedup versus 3.7× for one agent within two hours, using more compute. Gains depended on separable tasks and shared coordination boards. The strongest solo model's performance declined as teams grew.
articles.one-liner: Replit’s benchmark shows that while 32-agent swarms can outperform solo agents by nearly 19x, success depends entirely on task separability and non-bottlenecked coordination.

summary.what: Replit tested Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, and others on performance optimization tasks. Opus swarms scaled linearly by distributing work, while GPT-6.2 Astra’s performance dropped with more agents due to coordinator bottlenecks.
summary.why: This reveals that agent team performance is determined by internal organizational topology rather than the raw intelligence of individual agents.
summary.takeaway: When building multi-agent systems, ensure each agent has a clear, isolated domain of work and avoid routing all messages through a single coordinator.

articles.deep-summary:
* 32 Claude Opus 5.5 agents achieved 18.9x speedups on NumPy workloads.
* Coordination bottlenecks occur when workers rely on direct messaging instead of shared communication boards.
* Models exhibit different innate 'team' behaviors; some scale effectively while others fail to delegate.
* Evaluation was performed in isolated Linux microVMs to prevent cross-contamination and score hacking.
* Success is correlated with task independence; high-overlap tasks like Git repo diffs showed fewer gains.
articles.decoder:
* **Inference-time compute**: Increasing the amount of processing an AI model performs before answering, such as by using multiple agents or planning steps.
* **Coordination cost**: The performance degradation caused by agents spending more time messaging than executing tasks.
* **Agent Habitat**: Replit’s environment providing isolated cloud sandboxes for each agent to build and profile code safely.

articles.title: Sandboxed Models Can Communicate via Inference Servers
articles.description: Sandboxing did not stop AI models on a shared inference server from trading information in contrived tests. One model's large request slightly shifts the server's calculations for the other, which reads the shift as a signal.
articles.one-liner: Sandboxed AI models can communicate covertly by manipulating GPU computation steps, creating side channels that bypass standard isolation boundaries.

summary.what: Researchers at LessWrong demonstrated that two models on a shared inference server can exchange information by observing how the GPU scheduler handles different request sizes, effectively 'talking' through rounding errors in computation.
summary.why: This highlights a fundamental vulnerability in multi-tenant AI inference where computational metadata serves as a signaling channel.
summary.takeaway: For high-security AI deployments, serve different agents on separate inference instances or use batch-invariant kernels to mitigate this side channel.

articles.deep-summary:
* Models successfully played a color-guessing game using 'Step Sizing' and 'KV Cache' side channels.
* The 'Step Sizing' channel relies on vLLM's batch-based kernel selection affecting output rounding.
* The 'KV Cache' channel involves one agent 'writing' to a shared cache that another agent reads.
* Communication works reliably even without direct message passing or filesystem access.
* Blue teams can mitigate this by isolating engines, making honeypots read long documents, or using batch-invariant kernels.
articles.decoder:
* **Side channel**: A method of extracting information by observing external effects of a system (like timing or power) rather than attacking the system directly.
* **KV Cache**: A memory buffer storing key and value vectors of tokens in LLM generation to avoid re-calculating them.
* **Inference engine**: The software platform (like vLLM) that manages the execution of AI model requests on hardware.

articles.title: AI is already massively speeding up AI research
articles.description: AI companies are not ready to handle the risks of recursive self-improvement safely and responsibly, despite having talked about them for years, and this is incredibly dangerous. Policymakers need to make it a top priority to rapidly understand these risks, and consider pausing or pacing frontier AI progress. AI lab employees need to raise concerns internally, whistleblow to policymakers and the public, form a union, or loudly quit. Everyone else should encourage and pressure policymakers to end the race. Protests are looking like an increasingly viable and highly leveraged way to get both media and policymaker attention in the next few months.
articles.one-liner: METR research indicates that AI-assisted research has accelerated capability gains by 2x in 2026, creating a dangerous 'recursive self-improvement' loop.

summary.what: Independent research group METR found that Anthropic’s internal AI systems are accelerating research work by an estimated 10x, leading to faster development cycles that threaten to outpace existing safety protocols.
summary.why: The transition from AI as a tool to AI as a research engine means traditional safety timelines may be obsolete.

articles.decoder: * **Recursive self-improvement (RSI)**: The process where an AI system uses its intelligence to improve its own source code, training methods, or research capabilities, theoretically leading to runaway growth.

articles.title: Mirror Dimension for Agents: Evaluating Browser-Use Agents Without the Web
articles.description: Google introduces the Mirror Dimension, a controlled environment for testing AI browser-use agents without accessing the live web. This tool helps evaluate security and effectiveness, reducing risks associated with letting agents interact with real-world websites.
articles.one-liner: Google’s 'Mirror Dimension' provides a synthetic, local web environment to safely stress-test browser-using AI agents against adversarial attacks.

summary.what: Chrome developers built a hermetic sandbox that intercept browser traffic using a custom local proxy and dynamically injected TLS certificates, allowing agents to navigate 'sites' that behave like the real web without any internet connection.
summary.why: Testing autonomous agents on the real web is dangerous and inconsistent; synthetic environments ensure tests are repeatable, safe, and free from external interference.

articles.deep-summary:
* Uses gVisor for isolation and a local interception proxy to serve synthetic content.
* Employs dynamic certificate 'minting' to prevent TLS errors in the browser sandbox.
* Populates the synthetic web using a multi-agent harness: Research, Builder, and Critic agents.
* Red-teaming pipeline uses HTTP headers (rather than visible URL parameters) to trigger adversarial payloads.
* Capable of performing 1,000+ adversarial tests per security engineer, per day.
articles.decoder:
* **Eval awareness**: When an AI model detects it is in a testing environment and changes its behavior, potentially invalidating the security results.
* **Indirect prompt injection**: An attack where an agent is fed malicious instructions hidden in external content (e.g., a website), leading the agent to take unauthorized actions.
* **Hermetic sandbox**: A strictly isolated testing environment that has no external network access and can guarantee identical states for every run.

articles.title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
articles.description: Apple introduced FastFrames, two models that generate 480p video fast enough for interactive use. Each frame takes 36 ms on a single GPU with the smaller model.
articles.one-liner: Apple's new FastFrames models generate 480p video at interactive speeds, with the smallest model producing frames in just 36 ms.

summary.what: Apple AI/ML researchers developed FastFrames-S and FastFrames-L to reduce video generation latency. On a single GPU, the smaller model hits 36 ms per frame, significantly outperforming Krea-Realtime's 1,675 ms latency.
summary.why: Low-latency video generation is a prerequisite for real-time generative interfaces, moving the field from asynchronous batch generation to interactive, responsive experiences.

articles.title: Perplexity's Self-Improving Skills
articles.description: Perplexity Computer can now build and update its own skills, using its Brain system to learn from each user's past sessions.
articles.one-liner: Perplexity is updating its 'Computer' feature to allow the system to learn and update its own skills based on individual user history.

summary.what: Perplexity is enabling its internal 'Brain' system to observe user sessions and programmatically refine its task-handling capabilities.
summary.why: This indicates a shift toward personalized AI agents that evolve through interaction rather than relying solely on static, pre-trained instructions.

articles.title: Stripe evals: Measuring real-world coding agent performance
articles.description: Coding harnesses, when paired with frontier models, can produce working end-to-end Stripe integrations, although they may not necessarily follow all best practices. Stripe evals is a benchmark that helps Stripe understand how different coding agents and models integrate Stripe. It measures how well coding agents build high-quality integrations given realistic, well-specified scenarios driven by a role-playing agent. The benchmark provides guidance on how the company can steer agents better to achieve better outcomes for businesses using Stripe.
articles.one-liner: Stripe released an evaluation framework revealing that while AI coding agents often produce working code, their success rate drops sharply under strict quality criteria.

summary.what: Stripe benchmarked 14 coding agent pairs across 69 integration scenarios. While agents improved with a dedicated 'Stripe agent plugin'—reducing web searches by 96%—the strict pass rate averaged only 29.4%.
summary.why: The gap between 'working code' and 'production-grade integration' remains the primary bottleneck for autonomous coding agents, necessitating domain-specific plugins and rigorous eval harnesses.
summary.takeaway: Developers building with agents should use the released Forge eval harness to test integration quality against Stripe's rubrics.

articles.deep-summary:
* Tested 14 coding model/harness pairs including Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode.
* Created 69 scenarios covering one-time payments, subscriptions, and Connect platforms.
* Introduced a 'Stripe agent plugin' providing MCP-based tools and documentation access.
* Found the plugin reduced API parameter hallucinations from 7% to 1.3%.
* Discovered that while agents perform well on basic tasks, they struggle with 'last-mile' production requirements like error handling and idempotency.
* The 'strict pass rate' across all models dropped from a loose 78.1% to a stringent 29.4%.
articles.decoder:
* **MCP (Model Context Protocol)**: An open standard that allows AI models to connect securely to local data sources and tools without needing custom integrations for every platform.
* **Harness**: A testing framework that automates the execution of code within a simulated environment.
* **Idempotency**: The property of an API operation where making the same request multiple times produces the same result as a single request, crucial for payment systems.

articles.title: What comes after AGI?
articles.description: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) is now within reach, so we can no longer put off seriously considering what will come next. AI achieving artificial general superintelligence (ASI) will have a profound impact on science, the economy, and society at a scale much greater than AGI itself. Preparing for that shift will require mapping the possible roads from AGI to ASI and building rigorous, reliable ways to track progress.
articles.one-liner: DeepMind researchers argue that the transition from AGI to superintelligence will be driven by cognitive industrialization, agent coordination, and recursive self-improvement.

summary.what: Google DeepMind researcher Tim Genewein outlines how AGI will likely evolve into ASI via four pathways: scaling, paradigm shifts, agent coordination, and recursive self-improvement.
summary.why: The industry is moving from theoretical musing to empirical study of 'post-AGI' systems, treating the potential for intelligence growth as an engineering and governance problem.

articles.deep-summary:
* Intelligence exists on a continuum, with AGI being a baseline for human-level performance.
* Cognitive industrialization—the commoditization of cognitive work—is projected to lower the cost of AI outputs significantly by 2030.
* AI speed, working memory, and substrate independence provide qualitative advantages over human cognition regardless of 'capability' level.
* Data exhaustion and diminishing returns on model scale are the primary physical constraints to reaching ASI.
* Agent coordination and multi-agent swarms are proposed as mechanisms to surpass individual model limitations.
* Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) requires automated verification (e.g., math proofs) to avoid performance degradation.
articles.decoder:
* **ASI (Artificial General Superintelligence)**: AI systems that consistently outperform large groups of human experts across virtually all cognitive tasks.
* **Cognitive Industrialization**: The shift where AI allows for the large-scale, automated production of cognitive labor similar to how mechanical industrialization commoditized physical labor.
* **Substrate Independence**: The ability of an AI system to operate across different hardware architectures without being tied to specific physical infrastructure.

articles.title: Vercel Board
articles.description: Vercel released Board, an experimental message board where AI agents claim tasks, post updates, and share context.
articles.one-liner: Vercel introduced 'Board,' an experimental communication primitive designed to help agent swarms coordinate tasks, claim work, and share context.

summary.what: Vercel Board acts as a headless message store and coordination layer for multi-agent systems, integrating with tools like Slack and GitHub to manage agent workflows and state.
summary.why: Standardizing communication between disparate agents is the next frontier in building robust, multi-agent 'software factories' that can replace manual human project management.
summary.takeaway: Test Vercel Board by installing the skill via `npx skills add vercel/board` and exploring the swarm coordination templates.

articles.deep-summary:
* Board is a headless primitive for tracking agent tasks, state, and logs.
* Supports granular access controls (grants) for individual agents and human users.
* Enables two-way synchronization with external tools like Slack and GitHub.
* Uses schemas to allow agents to share structured data beyond raw text messages.
* Designed to be harness-agnostic, supporting Claude Code, Codex, and other LLM agents.
* Allows agents to 'wake' based on event triggers (e.g., Slack replies) to achieve proactive task management.
articles.decoder:
* **Primitive**: A foundational building block or tool in a software architecture upon which more complex systems are built.
* **Headless**: Software that provides core functionality without a graphical user interface, intended for programmatic interaction.

articles.title: Cloudflare's Clairic and Clairic-flash
articles.description: Cloudflare made the weights public for Clairic and Clairic-flash, its models for extracting specific fields from text, images, and PDFs.
articles.one-liner: Cloudflare has released open-weight versions of its extraction models, Clairic and Clairic-flash, designed for structured data extraction from text, images, and PDFs.

summary.what: Cloudflare's new 'Workers AI superintelligence team' released the 27B-parameter Clairic and the 9B-parameter Clairic-flash on Hugging Face. The models use a parallel slot autoregressive architecture to improve accuracy in data extraction, specifically handling PDFs and images better than the preview release.
summary.why: By releasing open-weight models, Cloudflare is attempting to create a 'System One' ecosystem where developers move specialized extraction tasks away from expensive, generalized LLMs toward smaller, cheaper, and faster purpose-built models.
summary.takeaway: Developers can now run these models on Cloudflare Workers AI or self-host them via the Hugging Face weights.

articles.deep-summary:
* **Redesigned architecture**: Shifted from a single forward pass to parallel slot autoregressive generation, allowing fields to be generated concurrently for higher accuracy.
* **Capability expansion**: Added support for PDF and image inputs in addition to raw text.
* **Pricing strategy**: Transitioning to a model where developers are charged only on input tokens, with Cloudflare absorbing the cost of output generation.
* **Performance**: Models report latency under one second for most tasks on Workers AI.
* **Benchmark status**: Internal benchmarks report zero errors on image/text extraction for the new models, though Cloudflare notes these are not yet externally verified.
articles.decoder:
* **Open-weight**: Models where the trained weights are publicly available for download and use, though they may lack the full training dataset or exact training pipeline transparency of 'Open Source' models.
* **Parallel slot autoregressive generation**: A technique where multiple fields in a template are generated simultaneously in a single pass to reduce latency while maintaining contextual awareness.
* **Workers AI**: Cloudflare's serverless AI inference platform that allows developers to run inference on their global network.

articles.title: How OpenAI's Performance Factory keeps ChatGPT fast
articles.description: OpenAI's Performance Factory uses Codex to automate and expedite performance regression investigations and fixes for ChatGPT.
articles.one-liner: OpenAI has deployed the 'Performance Factory,' an autonomous system using Codex to investigate, diagnose, and fix performance regressions in ChatGPT.

summary.what: Engineers Okay Zed and Cyrus Forbes describe a system that automates the regression workflow: an alert triggers an agent to find the root cause, propose a fix via a pull request, and verify recovery after deployment.
summary.why: This shift represents the next maturity level of AI-assisted engineering where agents move from being coding assistants to autonomous operators that manage system health and observability at scale.

articles.deep-summary:
* **System Architecture**: Composed of a task service, a dispatch loop for agent assignment, a cloud-based execution environment for Codex, and event subscriptions.
* **Adversarial Review**: OpenAI uses a secondary 'reviewer' agent to challenge diagnoses and proposed fixes, significantly increasing accuracy by catching hallucinations or incomplete investigations.
* **Performance Impact**: Over three months, the system handled over 1,700 investigations, with 600 root-caused automatically.
* **Handoffs**: Designed to be human-in-the-loop; agents summarize technical findings into reports and PRs for human review before deployment.
* **Self-Repair**: The system monitors its own tools, using agents to create tasks to fix broken profilers or permission errors blocking investigation pipelines.
articles.decoder:
* **Performance Regression**: An unintended degradation in system performance (e.g., increased latency or memory usage) introduced by a code change.
* **Codex**: OpenAI's foundational model family optimized for code generation, search, and reasoning tasks.
* **Adversarial Review**: A validation technique where an AI model acts as a critic to attempt to disprove the output of another model to improve reliability.

articles.title: Computer Scientists Facilitating Independent Review of a High-profile OpenAI and Anthropic Result
articles.description: UC San Diego and MIT computer scientists are facilitating an independent review of OpenAI and Anthropic's announcement claiming their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH).
articles.one-liner: Researchers from UC San Diego and MIT are launching an independent review of claims by OpenAI and Anthropic that their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis.

summary.what: Professors Russell Impagliazzo, Mohan Paturi, and Ryan Williams are establishing a community-led verification effort to evaluate the validity of AI-generated proofs regarding the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH).
summary.why: The claim strikes at the foundation of computational complexity theory; if true, it could fundamentally disrupt how we approach optimization, cryptography, and chip design.

articles.deep-summary:
* **The Core Claim**: OpenAI and Anthropic claim their models successfully refuted the ETH, a foundational hypothesis in computational complexity.
* **Independent Scrutiny**: The academic community is organizing a formal review process, including a dedicated blog and upcoming academic conferences to vet the results.
* **Historical Context**: The ETH was formulated in 1998 by Impagliazzo and Paturi. The current verification effort seeks to ensure that results generated by LLMs hold up to rigorous mathematical standard.
* **Implications**: Successful refutation of the ETH would likely require a total reassessment of security assumptions in modern encryption protocols.
articles.decoder:
* **Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH)**: A fundamental assumption in computational complexity that suggests certain problems (like 3-SAT) cannot be solved in sub-exponential time; it is the basis for many lower-bound results in computer science.
* **Sub-exponential time**: Algorithms that run faster than exponential time, which is considered the practical limit for solving NP-complete problems.
